2. Heard Mr.Mettu Goverdhan Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr.Bandi Venkata Srinivasulu, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, appearing on behalf of respondent No.1-State.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner, submitted that the petitioner has not committed the alleged offences and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

He further submitted that the petitioner and respondent No.2 were in a relationship and subsequent to the registration of the crime, the family members of both the petitioner and respondent No.2 solemnized their marriage as per Hindu rites and customs.
He further submitted that they are presently living together as husband and wife and have been blessed with a baby girl, namely Dadige Nainika, born on 15.02.2022, aged about three years.
4. He further submitted that the petitioner has filed I.A.Nos.3 and 4 of 2026 seeking permission to compound the offences and to record the compromise, respectively.

He further submitted that the Dadige Nagaraju @ Nani vs The Telangana State on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181213135/
1 parties are ready and willing to appear before the High Court Legal Services Committee.

sentences.text: 5. On 30.01.2026, when this Court raised a query as to whether it is permissible to record a compromise in cases involving heinous offences, the learned counsel for the petitioner requested this Court to direct the learned Additional Public Prosecutor to obtain instructions from the concerned Police Officer with regard to whether the petitioner and the victim are living together as husband and wife; whether their marriage was solemnized subsequent to the registration of the crime; and whether they have been blessed with a baby girl.

Pursuant to the same, on 11.03.2026,
learned counsel for the petitioner produced the marriage certificate and birth certificate of the child.

6. In view of the above said submissions, this Court vide order, dated 11.03.2026, directed the parties i.e., the petitioner and respondent No.2, to appear before the High Court Legal Services Committee, Hyderabad, on or before 20.03.2026 for their identification.

entities.text: High Court Legal Services Committee, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In compliance of the said order, the Secretary, High Court Legal Services Committee, has submitted report, dated 18.03.2026,
stating that the petitioner, and respondent No.2 were duly identified with copies of their Aadhar Cards.
It is further stated that the parties have willfully and without any coercion entered into compromise.
7. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor has not opposed the same.

8. In view of the said report and also in view of the compromise entered between the petitioner and respondent No.2 as well as the submissions made by the respective parties, I.A.Nos.3 and 4 of 2026 are allowed.

Consequently, the proceedings in S.C. No.569 of 2024 on the file of the Special Sessions Judge for Fast Tracking the Cases relating to Atrocities against Women-cum-XIII Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar, are hereby quashed against the petitioner/accused.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
9. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is allowed, subject to payment of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees five thousand only) to the High Court Legal Services Committee, Hyderabad and Rs.5,000/- (Rupees five thousand only) to the Telangana High Court Advocates Association, Hyderabad, by the petitioner, on or before 10.04.2026.
10.
